## Modelled probability and observed proportion {#l3-estimating-probability }

::: {.split }
::: {.column-block}

<h3>Theoretical</h3>

Based on a model of the outcomes.

For a fair coin:

$$P(H)=\frac12.$$

:::

::: {.column-block}

<h3>Experimental</h3>

Based on observations.

$$\widehat{P}(H)=\frac{\text{number of heads}}{\text{number of tosses}}.$$

:::
:::


::: {.takeaway}
Relative frequency is a practical estimate when no simple theoretical model is available.
:::
<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 49 · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
A hat indicates an estimate, not an exact theoretical probability. Coins in the simulator are modelled as fair and independent. Real trials also require stable conditions and a suitable sampling method.
:::
